name: Newberg
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Newberg, OR 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Newberg, OR: the tree lighting with Santa at the Chehalem Cultural Center, a holiday craft party, a Grinch breakfast and carols.
lede: Newberg starts its Christmas season the night after Thanksgiving, when Santa comes downtown and a giant Douglas fir lights up in front of the Chehalem Cultural Center, while the Newberg Scroll decorations glow on the light poles around town.
celebrates: The Newberg Downtown Coalition and Chehalem Park and Recreation District host the community tree lighting outside the Chehalem Cultural Center on East Sheridan Street, with photos with Santa, cookie decorating, a hot cocoa bar and a reindeer scavenger hunt for kids. CPRD adds a lights display on the Cultural Center building and grounds. Through December, Santa stops in at downtown businesses, and the December First Friday Art Walk fills the streets with art and music. George Fox University fills Bauman Auditorium with more than 150 student musicians for its Christmas Concert, and neighbors share a Christmas light route of decorated homes.
lastyear: In 2025 the Newberg tree lighting took place on Friday, November 28, in the plaza in front of the Chehalem Cultural Center. Santa arrived at 6 pm and the lighting followed 30 minutes later, with hot cocoa, carolers and a chance to share wish lists with Santa. CPRD decorated the Douglas fir, and the evening was a group effort of the Newberg Downtown Coalition, the city's public works department, the Noon Rotary Club and the Chehalem Valley Chamber of Commerce.
facts: The Newberg Scroll decorations on the town's poles date back to 1966, and the Newberg Fire Department's decorating tradition goes back to 1929, during the Great Depression. Each scroll is eight feet wide and four feet tall with three lit candlesticks. The originals burned in an August 1986 bowling alley fire and were back up by December. In 2026 Weyerhaeuser donated a 54-foot Douglas fir for the tree lighting, the first tree it has given.
trains: Newberg was once a stop on the Southern Pacific Red Electric. Electric passenger service on the Eastside line through Oswego, Tualatin and Newberg began on January 17, 1914, and it joined the Westside line north of McMinnville to form the 109-mile Yamhill Loop until passenger trains ended in 1929. Today the closest TriMet rail is WES Commuter Rail, a weekday line serving Beaverton, Tigard, Tualatin and Wilsonville. In Portland, families can ride the Holiday Express at the Oregon Rail Heritage Center and the Washington Park and Zoo Railway.

traditions: Santa arrives at the Chehalem Cultural Center the night after Thanksgiving, and the crowd counts down to the lighting of the community tree.
Lighted scrolls with three candlesticks have decorated Newberg's poles each season since 1966.
Choirs, orchestra, band and a theatre troupe share carols and the Christmas story in Bauman Auditorium.
Santa visits participating downtown businesses through December, so families can meet him while they shop.
Newberg neighbors decorate their homes and share a route that families can walk or drive.
The Chehalem Cultural Center invites families to make gingerbread villages, ornaments and cards.
kidfact: Newberg's lighted Christmas scrolls are eight feet wide. Firefighters used to practice carrying them up ladders to train for rescues.
faq: When is the Newberg Christmas tree lighting?

Newberg lights its community tree on the Friday after Thanksgiving in front of the Chehalem Cultural Center at 415 E Sheridan Street. The Newberg Downtown Coalition and Chehalem Park and Recreation District host it, with photos with Santa, cookie decorating, hot cocoa and a reindeer scavenger hunt. The coalition says the celebration and its activities are free.
What are the scroll decorations on Newberg's light poles?

They are the Newberg Scroll, holiday decorations that date back to 1966. Each is eight feet wide and four feet tall with three lit candlesticks. The Newberg Fire Department put them up for decades, and when the originals burned in a 1986 fire, new ones were made in time for December. Volunteers raised money to repair them in 2013.
Where does the Newberg Christmas tree come from?

For years Chehalem Park and Recreation District cut the tree from its own land at Bob and Crystal Rilee Park. In 2026 Weyerhaeuser donated a 54-foot Douglas fir, and CPRD and the City of Newberg Public Works Department raised it in front of the Chehalem Cultural Center in mid November, ahead of the lighting.
Is there a Christmas concert for families in Newberg?

Yes. George Fox University holds its annual Christmas Concert in Bauman Auditorium on the first weekend of December, with evening and afternoon performances. More than 150 student musicians from the choirs, band, orchestra and percussion ensemble take part, and student and child tickets cost less than adult tickets.
Did trains ever run to Newberg?

Yes. The Southern Pacific Red Electric ran electric passenger trains through Newberg starting in 1914, on the Eastside line through Oswego and Tualatin. It was part of the 109-mile Yamhill Loop that joined north of McMinnville. Passenger service ended in 1929.
